Dynamic matrices let the student choose one or both dimensions. Use
`mat{...}` only with `mode: custom`; the checker receives each named input as a
SymPy matrix at `response["inputs"][name]["matrix"]`.

::: {.callout-tip}
The controls never infer a dimension from the answer. Authors set neutral
initial dimensions and mathematical bounds. A dimension may be zero when its
minimum is zero.
:::

::: {#dynamic-matrix-method .math-exercise-context}

A matrix with $r$ rows and $c$ columns has shape $r\times c$. A $3\times0$
matrix has three rows and no columns; a $0\times2$ matrix has no rows and two
columns. These are legitimate matrix shapes. For a matrix $A$ with $n$
columns, a null-space basis matrix $Z$ must satisfy $AZ=0$, have linearly
independent columns, and have $n-\operatorname{rank}(A)$ columns. A set of
points on $y=2x$ consists of distinct row pairs $(x,2x)$. A zero matrix has
only zero entries, regardless of its rectangular shape.

:::

## 1. Choose the number of basis vectors

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-nullspace-basis
#| caption: A basis without announcing nullity
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       Z = response["inputs"]["Z"]["matrix"]
#|       C = Matrix([[1, 2, 3], [2, 4, 6]])
#|       contained = C * Z == zeros(C.rows, Z.cols)
#|       independent = Z.rank() == Z.cols
#|       complete = Z.cols == C.cols - C.rank()
#|       score = (int(contained) + int(independent) + int(complete)) / 3
#|       return {
#|           "score": score,
#|           "feedback": "Check that every column is in the null space, that the columns are independent, and that the basis is complete."
#|       }

Give a basis for the null space of
$C=\begin{bmatrix}1&2&3\\2&4&6\end{bmatrix}$. Enter the basis vectors as
columns of $Z$:

$Z=$ mat{name=Z, rows=3, cols=auto, initial-cols=1, min-cols=0, max-cols=3}
```

## 2. Choose the number of rows

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-point-rows
#| caption: A variable-length list of points
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       P = response["inputs"]["P"]["matrix"]
#|       on_line = all(simplify(P[i, 1] - 2*P[i, 0]) == 0 for i in range(P.rows))
#|       distinct = len({tuple(P.row(i)) for i in range(P.rows)}) == P.rows
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(on_line) + int(distinct)) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "Each row must be a point on y=2x, and the submitted points must be distinct."
#|       }

Give between two and four distinct points on the line $y=2x$, one point per
row:

$P=$ mat{name=P, rows=auto, cols=2, initial-rows=2, min-rows=2, max-rows=4}
```

## 3. Choose both dimensions

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-both-dimensions
#| caption: Any non-square zero matrix
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       A = response["inputs"]["A"]["matrix"]
#|       non_square = A.rows != A.cols
#|       zero = A == zeros(A.rows, A.cols)
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(non_square) + int(zero)) / 2,
#|           "feedback": "The matrix must be rectangular rather than square, and every entry must be zero."
#|       }

Give any non-square zero matrix with at least one row and one column:

$A=$ mat{name=A, rows=auto, cols=auto, initial-rows=2, initial-cols=1, min-rows=1, max-rows=4, min-cols=1, max-cols=4}
```

## 4. A correct matrix with zero columns

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-zero-columns
#| caption: The null-space basis of an invertible matrix
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       Z = response["inputs"]["Z0"]["matrix"]
#|       I = eye(2)
#|       contained = I * Z == zeros(2, Z.cols)
#|       independent = Z.rank() == Z.cols
#|       complete = Z.cols == 2 - I.rank()
#|       return {
#|           "score": (int(contained) + int(independent) + int(complete)) / 3,
#|           "feedback": "A basis matrix may have no columns when the null space contains only the zero vector."
#|       }

Give a basis for the null space of $I_2$. Enter basis vectors as columns:

$Z_0=$ mat{name=Z0, rows=2, cols=auto, initial-cols=1, min-cols=0, max-cols=2}
```

## 5. A correct matrix with zero rows

```{math-exercise}
#| label: dynamic-zero-rows
#| caption: A map into the zero-dimensional space
#| mode: custom
#| context: dynamic-matrix-method
#| checker: |
#|   def check(response, symbols):
#|       T = response["inputs"]["T"]["matrix"]
#|       return {
#|           "correct": T.rows == 0 and T.cols == 2,
#|           "feedback": "The matrix of a map from R² has two columns; a zero-dimensional codomain contributes no rows."
#|       }

Give the matrix of the unique linear map $T:\mathbb R^2\to\mathbb R^0$:

$[T]=$ mat{name=T, rows=auto, cols=2, initial-rows=1, min-rows=0, max-rows=3}
```
